title.narrative: Empoweing Women, Building Peace: Advancing Security and Equality in West Pokot, Elgeyo Marakwet and Baringo Counties
Empoweing Women, Building Peace: Advancing Security and Equality in West Pokot, Elgeyo Marakwet and Baringo Counties

description.narrative: Kenya has made significant strides in advancing the Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) agenda, particularly through its commitment to international frameworks such as the United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 (UNSCR 1325). Further, the 2010 Constitution of Kenya has provided a robust framework for promoting gender equality. Despite these advancements, Kenya faces substantial challenges in fully realizing the WPS agenda. The evaluation conducted by the Embassy in October – November 2022, identified the following factors that could inhibit KNAP WPS sustainability at the county level; Inadequate funding from the local county governments towards the operations of County Gender Sector Working Group (CGSWG) and - Intergovernmental Consultation Framework (IGCF); Weak link between national and county government through ICFG operationalization and funding structure; Rigid harmful cultural practices of FGM, GBV, cattle rustling, and armed conflict that is still prevalent in most of the counties; Droughts and shrinking natural resources could exacerbate conflict over resources. Despite these challenges, there are significant opportunities to advance the WPS agenda in West Pokot, Baringo, and Elgeyo Marakwet. The counties have a rich history of community-based conflict resolution mechanisms, such as elders' councils and peace committees, which can be strengthened and made more inclusive of women. Enhancing women’s participation in these traditional structures could lead to more sustainable and gender-sensitive peacebuilding efforts. Additionally, there is growing recognition of the importance of women’s leadership in peace and security at the national level, which can be leveraged to push for greater representation of women in local governance and conflict resolution, Targeted advocacy and education campaigns aimed at challenging harmful cultural practices and promoting gender equality can create an enabling environment for women’s increased involvement in peace and security. Objectives of the project: - To enhance the role and agency of grassroots women and women leaders as champions in decision-making processes, - To strengthen institutional capacity to implement legal and policy framework that support WPS agenda in West Pokot, Barino & Elgeyo Marakwet - To contribute to the eradication, prevention, and mitigation of Gender Based Violence among local communities in the 3 counties.
